text:
incident-bot: PAGER — automatic detection: sudden spike hitting /v1/embeddings and /v1/generate from clustered IP ranges. Severity: P2. Elevated token consumption + 5xx at edge. Paging SRE oncall @ravi. stack: edge-proxy -> apigw, suspect abusive scraping + credential reuse. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/edgespike

ravi: taking this. Can someone paste top IPs and user-agents?

ella: looking — top source ranges: 45.33.12.0/24, 103.21.55.0/24, and a handful from cloudprovider-x. User-agent: "python-requests/2.28" and a repeated UA: "ScraperBot/1.4". 10x normal embedding QPS, mostly tiny payloads.

matt: running kql on logs, seeing same API keys reused across clusters. Likely stolen keys being replayed with proxies. 401s are low; most are valid keys hitting quota.

kevin: quick mitigation proposal: (1) add temporary WAF rule to block UA pattern and top IP ranges (2) enable aggressive rate-slicing on /v1/embeddings for public tier (3) reduce batch size and disable batch endpoint for unidentified keys.

ravi: agreed. Apply WAF block + enforce per-key short token bucket. I'll make the change and monitor. Support: assign someone to notify suspected affected customers.

ella: WAF snippet I suggest (edge-config):

```
# block common scraper UA and top CIDRs
rule "block-scraperbot" {
  match_header("User-Agent", ".*ScraperBot.*") => BLOCK
}
rule "block-top-cidrs" {
  match_ip_cidr(["45.33.12.0/24","103.21.55.0/24"]) => BLOCK
}
```

kevin: also pushing rate-slice change in apigw:
```
endpoint: /v1/embeddings
policy:
  rate_limit: 30rps
  burst: 60
  scope: api_key
```

matt: applying a short-lived quota reduction for keys with anomalous pattern: drop to 10rps and throttle for 5m if >500 requests/min. Command: `curl -X POST https://internal-admin/api/keys/adjust -d '{"key":"<id>","rps":10,"window":"5m"}'`

support-lead: support assigned to triage potential customer impact. I see two keys tied to known customers (acct-acme, acct-locale) — will not throttle enterprise tenants without PM/CS approval. We'll throttle unknown/low-tier keys. Drafting customer notice for ACME in case they see degraded embedding throughput.

ravi: live deploy done: WAF rules active, rate-slice policy pushed to edge. Initial telemetry: embedding QPS down ~78% from those CIDRs, overall 30% drop in total embeddings traffic. 5xxs reduced.

oncall-bot: Oncall handoff reminder — @ravi to @simon in 20 minutes. Please document mitigations in incident channel.

simon: picking up in 20. Quick question: do we keep batch disable for public tier or roll back once traffic normalizes?

kevin: keep for at least 1 hour post-stable. Batches amplify throughput inefficiency and make abuse cheaper. We'll re-enable via canary after 1h.

support-lead: customer impact summary for execs:
- scope: broad scraper/proxy farm targeting embeddings and generate endpoints
- affected: mainly public-tier API keys; two known customers momentarily rate-limited (no data loss)
- mitigation: WAF blocks, per-key rate-slicing, temporary disable batch embeddings for non-enterprise keys
- ETA to revert: ~1-2 hours if stable; full rollback post-eval in 6-12 hours.

ravi: monitoring metrics: token burn stabilized, error budget good. We should watch for credential rotation attempts and new UA variations.

matt: warning — some attackers switching UAs and randomizing headers. We should add a secondary fingerprint: small-request-size + high-rate + repeated accept-language empty. I'll add a scoring rule to edge that increments a fingerprint score and quarantine if >3.

ella: added basic fingerprint scoring rule. Example predicate: `small_payload && rapid_qps && blank_accept_lang` -> score+1. Quarantine threshold 3 leads to temporary 10m block.

support-lead: CS will notify the two customers we throttled, explain protective action and offer immediate key rotate assistance. Draft message in #customer-comms for review.

ravi: simon — I'm leaving notes in the incident doc and flagging for postmortem if this repeats within 48h. Handoff in 10.

simon: got it. I'll keep an eye for UA churn and escalate to product if we need stricter default limits. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations holding, customer-impacts documented, oncall handed off to simon. Marking as MONITORED.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSE RECOMMENDED after 2h stable — if no recurrence, we'll close and open a followup postmortem ticket.

simon: closing note — after 90m no recurrence from primary CIDRs, reverting batch-disable only for vetted keys. WAF rules kept for 24h; will review tomorrow and schedule automated key-rotation detection.

support-lead: postmortem ticket created: https://pm.redwood.example/tickets/INC-2475 — assigned to eng-sre/matt for root cause and longer-term mitigation (better key hygiene + automated suspected-key rotation).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: all alerts quiet. Great job coordinating. :tada:
